title: Quandela Expands International Photonic Footprint with Deployment Alliance in Qatar and Foundry MoU in Taiwan - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Quandela signed two deals: a tripartite alliance with Mekdam Holding Group and MEEZA to deploy cloud and on-prem photonic quantum systems in sovereign Gulf data centers, and an MoU with Taiwan's Hermes-Epitek to co-develop and industrialize integrated photonic quantum hardware combining its quantum-dot sources with Hermes-Epitek SNSPDs.

insights.claim: Quandela entered a tripartite partnership with Qatar-listed Mekdam Holding Group and data center provider MEEZA to deploy cloud and on-premises photonic quantum systems across Gulf Cooperation Council states.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gulf sovereign-tech budgets are becoming a customer base for European quantum vendors.
insights.locator: In Qatar, Quandela entered a tripartite

insights.claim: The Quandela-Mekdam-MEEZA alliance expands a June 2026 agreement to set up a Quandela-Mekdam Quantum Center of Excellence in Doha and integrates Quandela platforms into MEEZA's sovereign data centers for fault-tolerant computing, quantum machine learning and workforce certification aligned with Qatar National Vision 2030.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Escalation from a center of excellence to data-center integration indicates deepening commitment; watch for disclosed contract values.
insights.locator: In Qatar, Quandela entered a tripartite

insights.claim: Quandela's deployment model in Qatar pairs its quantum-dot photonic architectures with regional data center partners, framing quantum as sovereign infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sovereign data-residency demand is a selling point for on-prem QPUs over hyperscaler cloud access.
insights.locator: European photonic quantum computing developer Quandela

insights.claim: Quandela signed an MoU with Taiwan-based semiconductor equipment and quantum foundry supplier Hermes-Epitek Corporation to co-develop and industrialize integrated photonic quantum hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Photonic quantum players are tapping Taiwan's semiconductor ecosystem for manufacturing scale.

insights.claim: The initial Quandela-Hermes-Epitek R&D phase combines Quandela's semiconductor quantum-dot single-photon sources and photonic integrated circuits with Hermes-Epitek's superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) and cryogenic systems on a fiber-coupled testbed in Taiwan.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Detectors and cryogenics are key bottleneck components for photonic QC; securing a supplier partner de-risks scale-up.

insights.claim: A subsequent joint Quandela-Hermes-Epitek system installation is contemplated but remains subject to definitive agreements.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: MoU is non-binding; track conversion to a definitive agreement.
